title: Case Report: Laser thermal ablation for severe primary hyperparathyroidism in a pregnant patient with MEN1 syndrome.
abstract: Primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) during pregnancy is a rare clinical entity associated with substantial maternal and fetal morbidity, particularly when complicated by severe hypercalcemia. We present the case of a 44-year-old multigravida at 27 + 5 weeks' gestation who presented with symptomatic, severe hypercalcemia (3.12 mmol/L), and acute kidney injury. Diagnostic evaluation confirmed bilateral parathyroid lesions. Due to high surgical risk and patient refusal of traditional parathyroidectomy, ultrasound-guided laser thermal ablation (LTA) of the dominant right inferior adenoma was performed. The procedure induced a rapid reduction in parathyroid hormone (PTH) concentrations and normalization of serum calcium levels, accompanied by a marked recovery of renal function. Subsequent genetic testing identified a pathogenic MEN1 mutation, confirming multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1. At 39 weeks of gestation, the patient delivered a healthy infant via elective cesarean section, with no evidence of neonatal hypocalcemia. This case demonstrates that LTA may serve as a safe, effective, and minimally invasive alternative for managing severe PHPT in pregnancy when conventional surgery is contraindicated or declined. To our knowledge, this represents the first reported application of LTA in this specific clinical scenario.

title: Resistance to thyroid hormone alpha associated with a novel THRA ligand-binding domain variant: familial clinical, biochemical, skeletal, and exploratory cerebral FDG-PET/CT metabolic findings.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thyroid hormones (TH) regulate skeletal development, central nervous system maturation, and energy homeostasis, primarily through the nuclear receptors TRα and TRβ, encoded by the THRA and THRB genes. Pathogenic variants in THRA lead to resistance to thyroid hormone alpha (RTHα), a rare and diagnostically challenging condition.
METHODS: A 36-year-old woman and her 12-year-old son were studied to characterize the clinical, biochemical, radiological, and exploratory cerebral metabolic findings associated with a previously unreported, likely pathogenic variant in THRA. Both individuals underwent a comprehensive clinical evaluation. Thyroid function tests included TSH, fT4, fT3, TT3, TT4, and rT3, along with additional biochemical assessments.Molecular analysis included whole-exome sequencing in proband 1, which identified a variant in THRA (NM_199334.5:c.662T>C; p.Ile221Thr), subsequently confirmed in the second case. Additionally, the adult patient underwent brain positron emission tomography with 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG PET) to assess regional cerebral metabolism with exploratory visual and ROI-based comparison with an age- and sex-matched control subject.
RESULTS: Both patients exhibited a phenotype consistent with RTHα, characterized by hypotonia, macrocephaly, dysmorphic features, chronic constipation, and normocytic anemia. The fT3/fT4 ratio was elevated (high-normal), and rT3 levels were decreased in both cases. The THRA variant was located in the ligand-binding domain and segregated with the familial phenotype. Exploratory brain ^18F-FDG PET assessment in Proband 1 showed symmetrically higher FDG uptake in the prefrontal cortex, basal ganglia, and lateral temporal cortex compared with the control subject, with consistently higher SUVmax values across the evaluated ROIs. These findings represent an exploratory single-subject comparison and have not previously been reported in RTHα.
CONCLUSIONS: This study expands the clinical, biochemical, radiological, and metabolic spectrum associated with THRA variants and suggests that cerebral metabolic evaluation may provide additional diagnostic insights in RTHα. Further studies, including larger cohorts and functional analyses, will be necessary to confirm the proposed mechanisms and the clinical relevance of the observed metabolic findings.

title: Real-world effectiveness of liraglutide in children with type 2 diabetes.
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Since liraglutide's approval for the treatment of type 2 diabetes (T2D) in children, no real-world studies have examined its clinical outcomes in adolescents.
OBJECTIVE: Compare hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) changes in adolescents with T2D taking liraglutide in a clinical setting.
DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study from 2020 to 2023.
PARTICIPANTS: Patients with T2D ages <18 years who were prescribed liraglutide. Patients were divided into 2 groups: treated (those with evidence of taking liraglutide for ≥26 weeks) and control (those prescribed but who did not take liraglutide).
MAIN OUTCOMES: Changes in HbA1c after 26 weeks of treatment were calculated. Secondary outcomes included HbA1c changes after 52 weeks, and body mass index (BMI) z score changes and lipid markers at 26 and/or 52 weeks.
RESULTS: There was a strong trend toward a decrease in HbA1c after 26 weeks of liraglutide treatment compared with control (-0.40 [-1.90, 0.20] vs +0.15 [-1.30, 0.88], P = .064; n = 85 vs n = 30); no difference was observed at 52 weeks (-0.20 [-1.23,0.93] vs 0.50 [-1.13,1.70], P = .15; n = 100 vs n = 44). BMI z score was stable in both groups, with no differences between groups. Lipid levels were available in a small subset of patients. The liraglutide-treated group had a decrease in total cholesterol (-0.21 [-0.60, 0.16] mmol/L vs 0.49 [0.06, 0.76] mmol/L, P = .005; n = 36 vs n = 12) and low-density lipoprotein (-0.23 [-0.56, 0.16] mmol/L vs 0.35 [0.14, 0.63] mmol/L, P < .01; n = 31 vs n = 12) vs control.
CONCLUSION: Liraglutide shows potential benefits for lowering HbA1c and cholesterol in children with T2D in a clinical setting. Additional work is needed to understand how to optimize HbA1c improvements with liraglutide.

title: Limited Predictive Value of Genotype in GNAS-Related Disorders: Phenotypic Variability in a Cohort of 36 Pediatric Patients.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pseudohypoparathyroidism (PHP) and related GNAS-associated disorders are rare conditions characterized by marked clinical and biochemical heterogeneity. Genotype-phenotype correlations remain complex due to genomic imprinting and parent-of-origin effects.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate genotype-phenotype correlations and intrafamilial variability in pediatric patients with GNAS-related disorders, with particular emphasis on familial cases.
METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted in 36 patients (20 females, 16 males) from 22 unrelated families diagnosed with GNAS-related disorders. Genetic analysis included next-generation sequencing and, in selected cases, methylation studies. Variants were classified as confirmed loss-of-function (LOF), predicted LOF, or non-LOF according to ACMG criteria and in silico splice prediction. For genotype-phenotype analyses, predicted LOF variants were included in the LOF group. Clinical, biochemical, and anthropometric data were analyzed, and pedigree analysis was performed to assess inheritance patterns and intrafamilial variability.
RESULTS: Genetic or epigenetic alterations involving the GNAS locus were identified in 26 of 36 patients (72.2%), including sequence variants in 24 patients and methylation defects in 2 patients. In 10 patients (27.8%), no molecular abnormality was identified, either due to lack of genetic testing or negative results. Among the 24 patients with sequence variants, 17 carried confirmed LOF variants according to ACMG classification. For genotype-phenotype analyses, two additional patients carrying the splice-region variant c.312+5G>A, predicted to impair splicing based on concordant predictions from multiple in silico tools, were included in the LOF group, resulting in a total of 19 LOF and 5 non-LOF patients. Patients with LOF variants demonstrated a significantly more severe biochemical phenotype, including higher PTH levels (p = 0.039), lower calcium levels (p = 0.018), higher phosphate levels (p = 0.013), and lower fT4 levels (p = 0.014). No significant differences were observed in TSH, BMI SDS, or height SDS. Pedigree analysis revealed marked intrafamilial variability, even among individuals carrying identical variants. Maternal inheritance predominated in familial cases. Notably, a clinically affected family without molecular confirmation was identified based on pedigree analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: GNAS-related disorders demonstrate substantial phenotypic variability both between and within families. Loss-of-function variants are associated with a more severe biochemical phenotype, whereas clinical features are less discriminatory. Maternal inheritance predominates, consistent with imprinting mechanisms. Although loss-of-function variants were associated with a more severe biochemical phenotype, substantial inter- and intrafamilial variability limited the predictive value of genotype alone. These findings highlight the importance of integrated clinical, biochemical, and genetic evaluation, particularly in familial cases.

title: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus And Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease In Children And Adolescents: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to determine the prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) using vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE), and to evaluate associated clinical and laboratory features.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 72 children with T1DM and 83 healthy controls who were comparable in age and sex. Hepatic steatosis was assessed using ultrasonography and VCTE. A controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) value >236 dB/m was used to define CAP-based hepatic steatosis/MASLD in the T1DM group. Clinical, anthropometric, laboratory, and radiological characteristics were compared between groups. Correlations of CAP and liver stiffness measurement (LSM) with clinical and laboratory parameters were evaluated in the T1DM cohort. Stepwise multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to identify candidate factors independently associated with CAP and LSM values.
RESULTS: CAP-based hepatic steatosis/MASLD was more frequent in children with T1DM than in controls (31.9% vs. 14.5%). Among children with T1DM, those with MASLD had higher body mass index, WHtR, diastolic blood pressure, and triglyceride levels than those without MASLD. In the multivariable CAP model, diabetes duration, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and WHtR were independently associated with higher CAP values. WHtR and alanine aminotransferase were independently associated with higher LSM values.
CONCLUSION: Children and adolescents with T1DM had a higher prevalence of CAP-based hepatic steatosis/MASLD than healthy controls. Adiposity-related parameters and dyslipidemia appear to be important clinical features associated with hepatic steatosis in pediatric T1DM.

title: Early childhood changes in BMI z-score and serum IGF-1 levels at age 6 years: the Japan environment and children study.
abstract: Body mass index (BMI) is associated with insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) concentrations in children, but longitudinal evidence regarding BMI changes during early childhood and IGF-1 concentrations at age 6 years remains limited. We examined associations between early childhood BMI z-score changes and serum IGF-1 concentrations at age 6 years in 2757 children from the Japan Environment and Children's Study. BMI z-scores were assessed at ages 2, 4, and 6 years, and serum IGF-1 was measured at age 6 years. Associations of overall BMI z-score change from ages 2 to 6 years and interval-specific changes from ages 2 to 4 and 4 to 6 years with IGF-1 were examined using multivariable linear regression. Longitudinal associations of repeated BMI z-scores with thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), free thyroxine (FT4), and 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models. Overall BMI z-score change from ages 2 to 6 years was positively associated with IGF-1 (B = 18.14 ng/mL; 95% confidence interval [CI], 16.34-19.95; P < .001). When interval-specific changes were simultaneously modeled, changes from ages 2 to 4 years (B = 11.43; 95% CI, 8.82-14.15) and 4 to 6 years (B = 21.24; 95% CI, 18.94-23.54) were both associated with IGF-1 (both P < .001). Associations with TSH and FT4 were weaker and inconsistent, while the age-dependent association with 25(OH)D was attenuated after adjustment for season of blood collection. These findings suggest that changes in body size during early childhood are associated with variation in serum IGF-1 concentrations at school age.

title: The diagnostic journey of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva: evidence from a national cohort of 114 patients.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP) is an ultra-rare genetic disorder caused by gain-of-function variants in ACVR1, characterized by congenital great-toe malformations, recurrent inflammatory soft-tissue swellings, and progressive heterotopic ossification (HO). Early lesions may resemble neoplastic, inflammatory, infectious, or trauma-related conditions, whereas invasive procedures can trigger additional HO.
METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional analysis of 114 patients with molecularly confirmed FOP enrolled in the National Rare Diseases Registry System of China. The diagnostic journey was reconstructed to evaluate diagnostic delay, misdiagnosis, missed diagnostic opportunities, and patient-reported outcomes after high-risk procedures.
RESULTS: Patients were recruited from 23 provinces or regions. Diagnostic delay exceeded 3 years in 34.5% patients and 10 years in 9.7% patients. FOP was not considered at the first hospital visit in 85 of 114 patients (74.6%), and 72 of 114 (63.2%) reported misdiagnosis. Among misdiagnosed patients, tumor-related diagnoses were most common (36/72, 50.0%), followed by orthopedic or congenital (13/72, 18.1%) and inflammatory or infectious diagnoses (12/72, 16.7%). 102 of 114 patients (89.5%) reported congenital great-toe malformation. Biopsy was reported by 51 patients (44.7%), of whom 41 (80.4%) reported subsequent worsening; 22 of 25 patients (88.0%) who underwent HO excision reported recurrence or new lesions at the surgical site.
CONCLUSION: Diagnostic errors remained common in FOP. Biopsy and HO excision were also frequently reported in FOP patients and were often followed by patient-reported worsening or recurrence. These findings provide a rationale for prospective evaluation of an early-recognition pathway emphasizing examination of the great toes, avoidance of invasive procedures when FOP is suspected, ACVR1 testing, and specialist referral.

title: Exploring genetic variants in premature ovarian insufficiency: a cohort-based investigation of monogenic etiologies.
abstract:
CONTEXT: Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI), affecting about 3.5% of women under 40, is marked by menstrual irregularities, amenorrhea, and heterogeneous pubertal development. Although next-generation sequencing (NGS) has expanded the list of POI-associated genes, most cases remain unexplained, and the clinical diagnostic value of gene panels is still insufficiently assessed.
OBJECTIVE: This study combines a cohort-based analysis with a critical methodological reassessment of NGS diagnostic yield in POI.
DESIGN: Prospective multicenter observational cohort study (2016-2023).
SETTING: Three Belgian academic hospitals.
PATIENTS: One hundred sixty unrelated women with idiopathic POI and 716 female controls.
INTERVENTION: Targeted NGS of 155 POI-associated genes. Variants were classified following American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association for Molecular Pathology guidelines, and genes were evaluated using the latest gene-disease relationship (GDR) scoring framework.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Identification of pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants (primary outcome). Diagnostic yield of the gene panel based on genes with strong evidence (secondary outcome).
RESULTS: Pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants were identified in 19.3% of patients; however, only 7.5% were considered clinically relevant based on gene validity and inheritance patterns. Limiting analysis to the 40 genes with the strongest GDR evidence yielded a 4.4% diagnostic rate. Adding 10 genes supported by recent literature increased the yield to 7.5%. In patients with primary amenorrhea, the diagnostic rate reached 15.4%. These findings highlight the gap between variant burden and true diagnostic yield in POI.
CONCLUSION: Targeted NGS panels provide valuable clinical insight into POI genetics but should be complemented with broader genomic approaches for comprehensive diagnosis.

title: Somapacitan Treatment in Children and Adolescents Born SGA: Two-Year Efficacy and Preference Over Daily GH.
abstract:
CONTEXT: Children born small for gestational age (SGA) without spontaneous catch-up growth may require GH treatment; however, daily injections are burdensome. Somapacitan is a once-weekly long-acting GH.
OBJECTIVE: To assess efficacy and safety of once-weekly somapacitan in children born SGA, including outcomes after switching from daily GH.
DESIGN: REAL8 is a randomized, multinational, open-label, active-controlled phase 3 study with a 52-week main period and 104-week extension (NCT05330325). REAL9 (NCT05723835) is a multinational, open-label, uncontrolled phase 3 study.
SETTING: Clinics across Europe, Asia, and the Americas.
PARTICIPANTS: REAL8 randomized 142 GH-treatment-naïve, prepubertal children born SGA; 141 received treatment and 139 completed 104 weeks. REAL9 enrolled 12 children/adolescents born SGA (GH-naïve or previously treated).
INTERVENTIONS: In REAL8, participants were randomized (2:1:1) to somapacitan 0.24 mg/kg/week or daily GH (0.035 or 0.067 mg/kg/day) for 52 weeks; all received 0.24 mg/kg/week somapacitan in weeks 52-104. In REAL9, participants received 0.24 mg/kg/week somapacitan for 26 weeks.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Annualized height velocity (HV); secondary outcomes included height SD score (HSDS).
RESULTS: In REAL8, mean HV during weeks 52-104 remained above baseline across groups (8.5-8.8 cm/year), including after switching from daily GH; HSDS increased through week 104, and IGF-I SDS were similar between groups. In REAL9, HV increased in GH-naïve participants and was maintained in previously treated participants. Somapacitan was well-tolerated; adverse events were mostly mild and injection-site reactions were infrequent. Most participants switching from daily GH preferred somapacitan.
CONCLUSIONS: In children born SGA, once-weekly somapacitan maintained efficacy through 2 years, with safety comparable to daily GH, and was preferred after switching.

title: Novel ABCC2 mutations in a neonate with Dubin-Johnson syndrome: a case report.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dubin-Johnson syndrome (DJS) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the ABCC2 gene, leading to impaired excretion of conjugated bilirubin. Neonatal or infantile onset is uncommon and easily misdiagnosed as biliary atresia or progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis.
CASE PRESENTATION: We report a female infant who presented with persistent jaundice since birth (onset in the neonatal period, ≤28 days). A definitive genetic diagnosis of Dubin-Johnson syndrome (DJS) was established at 11 months of age through next-generation sequencing. Her subsequent 5-year follow-up indicates a favorable clinical course. Laboratory tests revealed consistently normal transaminase levels with elevated total bilirubin (peak 120.3 μmol/L at 52 days), direct bilirubin (peak 61.3 μmol/L), and gamma-glutamyl transferase (88 U/L). Next-generation sequencing identified two novel compound heterozygous mutations in the ABCC2 gene: c.2443C>T (p.R815X, nonsense) inherited from the mother and c.4465_4473delinsGGCCCACAG (p.1489_1491delinsGPQ, in-frame) inherited from the father. Both mutations were classified as pathogenic/likely pathogenic according to ACMG guidelines (c.2443C>T: PVS1, PM2, PM3; c.4465_4473delinsGGCCCACAG: PM2, PM3, PM4) and have not been previously reported. Ursodeoxycholic acid therapy was administered, and bilirubin levels showed progressive decline over time; however, this improvement may also reflect the spontaneous trend toward resolution that is characteristic of the natural history of DJS.
CONCLUSION: This case expands the mutational spectrum of ABCC2 gene and highlights the critical role of genetic testing in early diagnosis of infantile DJS, thereby avoiding unnecessary invasive procedures. The favorable prognosis with conservative management further supports the benign nature of this condition.

title: Effects of combined GnRHa and letrozole on serum steroid profiles in girls with advanced bone age.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of combined GnRHa and letrozole on serum steroid profiles (classical, 11-oxygenated, and backdoor androgen pathways) in girls with advanced bone age, and to monitor adverse events.
METHODS: 28 girls with advanced bone age were enrolled. Of these, 15 received add-on letrozole after GnRHa monotherapy (Group B); the remaining 13 started combination therapy from baseline (Group A). Blood was collected at baseline, 1, and 6 months. Steroids were measured by LC-MS/MS.
RESULTS: At baseline, Group A had higher classical androgens, progestogens, estrogens, INB, SHBG, and FAI than Group B (all P < 0.05), while 11-oxygenated androgens were similar. In Group A, classical androgens, P, 17-OHP, 5α-DHP, 17OH-DHP, 3α-diol, E1, E2, and FAI decreased markedly (all overall P < 0.01) and remained lower at 6 months; 11-KT showed a modest reduction at 1 month (P = 0.02), but other 11-oxygenated androgens were unchanged. In Group B, add-on letrozole reduced E1, E2, AMH, and INB (all overall P < 0.05), while most androgens and progestogens were stable. No hyperandrogenism or adverse events were observed.
CONCLUSIONS: Over 6 months, combined GnRHa and letrozole was not associated with hyperandrogenism in girls with advanced bone age. In Group A, gonadal androgens and estrogens were markedly suppressed, while adrenal androgens remained stable. In Group B, add-on letrozole had limited effects on most androgens. Estrogen suppression was observed in both groups. These findings appear to support short-term safety, although longer-term data are needed.

title: Inpatient continuous glucose monitoring halves the risk of hypoglycemia in patients with hyperinsulinism.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Patients with congenital hyperinsulinism (HI) face recurrent and unpredictable hypoglycemia. Conventional inpatient monitoring relies on intermittent fingerprick glucose testing, which is burdensome for pediatric patients and risks missing hypoglycemic episodes between tests.Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) provides high granularity, complimentary monitoring but with unproven efficacy to detect and reduce hypoglycemia in the inpatient setting. This study evaluates whether CGM can improve inpatient safety through the early detection, and subsequent treatment, of hypoglycemic episodes.
METHODS: Thirteen inpatients with HI were monitored using Dexcom G7 or G6 device. Finger-prick glucose monitoring was performed at the expert clinician's discretion and to verify CGM-prompted hypoglycemia alerts. All CGM data were retrospectively searched for hypoglycemia episodes. Fingerprick glucose data were concurrently analysed, alongside electronic health records, to quantify early hypoglycemia detection and subsequent hypoglycemia saved. CGM accuracy was analysed using established metrics, including hypoglycemia sensitivity and error grid analysis, in Python 3.1.1.
RESULTS: From 3504 paired CGM and fingerprick values, hypoglycemia sensitivity was 56.7%, with CGM devices tending to overread, by a mean of +0.43mmol/L. On Hypoglycemia Error Grid analysis, 6.2% of values were classed as moderate or severe risk.Patient data, from 627 days of monitoring, showed 721 CGM-detected hypoglycemia events (<3.5 mmol/L). Of these, 448 (62.1%) were refuted as false positives and 273 (37.9%) were confirmed as true hypoglycemia, by fingerprick glucose monitoring. Patients spent a mean of 16 minutes/day (1.1% time) in hypoglycemia. CGM alerts saved an estimated mean of 21 minutes/day of hypoglycemia; a more than halving of total hypoglycemia experienced per patient.
DISCUSSION: The use of CGM within the inpatient setting, for those with HI, allows for a significant reduction in hypoglycemia; potentially halving hypoglycemic time. Sensor accuracy remains poor in the inpatient setting, resulting in high false negatives and suboptimal hypoglycemia sensitivity.However, the overall burden of CGM use is relatively low in the inpatient setting, when healthcare professionals can share the work with parents.

title: Long-term endocrine and reproductive outcomes in female adolescent and young adult survivors after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation for hematological malignancies during childhood or adolescence.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer treatment during childhood and adolescence, particularly hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), may adversely affect long-term reproductive and endocrine health in female adolescent and young adult (AYA) survivors, leading to premature ovarian insufficiency (POI), which may be associated with impaired pubertal development, low bone mass, and reproductive complications.
METHODS: This study included 34 female survivors treated with HSCT for hematological malignancies during childhood or adolescence (median age 10.8 years). The median follow-up from HSCT to the last gynecological assessment was 8.5 years. Hormonal assessment, pelvic ultrasound, and bone mineral density (BMD) evaluation were performed. Patients were classified as having normal ovarian function, transient ovarian insufficiency (TOI), or persistent POI.
RESULTS: At the last follow-up, normal ovarian function was observed in 15 patients (44.1%), TOI in 7 (20.6%), and persistent POI in 12 (35.3%). Patients with normal ovarian function were significantly older at HSCT (p = 0.0432), whereas premenarchal status was associated with impaired ovarian outcome (p = 0.0066). In multivariable analysis including cyclophosphamide equivalent dose (CED), radiotherapy, and menarchal status at HSCT, postmenarchal status was associated with markedly lower odds of ovarian insufficiency (adjusted OR 0.056, 95% CI 0.005-0.566; p = 0.0147). All postmenarchal patients received GnRHa, precluding separation of the effects of menarchal status and GnRHa exposure; GnRHa-treated survivors had higher AMH concentrations (p =0.0032). AMH and FSH concentrations differed significantly between groups (both p < 0.01). Uterine and mean ovarian volumes, antral follicle count (AFC), and BMD were significantly lower in patients with TOI and POI (all p < 0.05). Radiotherapy exposure was associated with both lower uterine and ovarian volumes, while puberty induction was also associated with lower uterine volume (all p <0.05). Two patients diagnosed with POI achieved spontaneous pregnancies during follow-up, one resulting in a live birth.
CONCLUSIONS: Ovarian dysfunction is highly prevalent after childhood HSCT, although partial recovery of ovarian function may occur even in patients with a diagnosis of POI. Persistent POI is associated with impaired uterine development and lower BMD despite ongoing hormone replacement therapy, underscoring the need for timely and long-lasting individualized endocrine and reproductive care in AYA survivors.

title: Towards precision medicine in diabetes: pharmacogenomic approaches for MODY and type 2 diabetes with insights from GLIS3 gene variants.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diabetes mellitus encompasses a heterogeneous group of metabolic disorders with a significant genetic basis that current standardized treatment protocols fail to adequately address. Type 2 diabetes in particular is driven by genetic factors that operate independently of lifestyle, with a substantial proportion of patients in South Asian populations developing the disease despite normal body weight and healthy habits. India presents a uniquely important context for pharmacogenomic research given its extraordinary population stratification across tribal, linguistic, religious, and geographic groups creating a genetic landscape that Western genomic data cannot adequately represent.
OBJECTIVE: This review evaluates pharmacogenomic evidence across monogenic and polygenic diabetes subtypes, presents Indian clinical case studies demonstrating the consequences of genomic misclassification, and positions GLIS3 as an underexplored regulatory gene with cross-disease relevance spanning neonatal diabetes, Type 1, and Type 2 diabetes. It further examines the potential for expanded clinical implementation of genotype-guided therapy, particularly in genetically diverse populations.
KEY INSIGHTS: GLIS3 encodes a zinc finger transcription factor that governs beta-cell development, insulin gene transcription, and endoplasmic reticulum stress protection by functioning as a master regulator of beta-cell survival rather than acting through a single pathway. Its association across multiple diabetes subtypes, combined with emerging evidence of population-specific variants in Indian cohorts, positions it as a compelling future pharmacogenomic target. However, no GLIS3-directed clinical testing or therapy is currently available, and its pharmacogenomic utility remains hypothetical pending prospective validation. Indian pharmacogenomic data further reveal 76 known variants affecting antidiabetic drug response, with higher frequencies of poor metformin response alleles compared to global population findings with immediate clinical implications for one of the world's highest diabetes-burden nations.
CONCLUSION: Realizing the potential of precision medicine in diabetes requires population-specific genomic research, integration of pharmacogenomic testing into national health schemes such as Ayushman Bharat, development of AI-driven clinical decision tools, and policy frameworks guided by bodies such as ICMR. Genotype-guided therapy represents an emerging clinical priority with the potential to improve outcomes in genetically diverse populations where standardized protocols may be suboptimal.

title: Short and long-term outcomes after gestational diabetes diagnosis using different glycemic criteria: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
CONTEXT: Lower gestational diabetes (GDM) diagnostic criteria on an oral glucose tolerance test are widely recommended, but their impacts on maternal, neonatal, long-term and economic outcomes remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To compare outcomes after GDM diagnosis using lower versus higher diagnostic strategies.
METHODS: We searched for randomized controlled trials (RCT) and prospective cohort studies comparing outcomes following assessment for GDM and treatment if indicated, using lower versus higher glycemic diagnostic criteria or thresholds in four databases and four trial registries (PROSPERO registration CRD420251183179) to 27th July 2026. Two reviewers independently assessed risk of bias, conducted random-effects meta-analyses and evaluated GRADE certainty.
RESULTS: Seventeen studies were included, with nine RCTs and one cohort study contributing to the meta-analysis (81,528 women). Lower diagnostic criteria or thresholds, compared with higher diagnostic criteria or thresholds, doubled GDM diagnosis and pharmacotherapy use, increased neonatal hypoglycemia (RCTs: 18 more per 1,000; 95% CI 11 to 25 more) and maternal-neonatal separation (RCTs: 6 more per 1,000; 95% CI 1 to 12 more), but had little to no effect on other short-term outcomes. Longer-term evidence was limited to follow-up of one RCT reporting reduced maternal hypertension and child neurodevelopmental impairment but increased subsequent GDM at five-year follow-up with use of lower criteria or thresholds. Findings on GDM-related healthcare costs were inconsistent, with no long-term economic data.
CONCLUSIONS: Lower diagnostic criteria increased the diagnosis of GDM and some aspects of healthcare utilization, without improving short-term outcomes. Limited evidence suggested possible longer-term benefits, warranting further long-term follow-up from high-quality RCTs.

journal.title: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism

title: Interpretable machine learning identifies predictors of IGF-1 during growth hormone therapy in boys.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) is widely used to guide growth hormone (GH) therapy, yet its predictors during the maintenance phase and puberty remain incompletely understood. We aimed to predict IGF-1 standard deviation scores (SDS) at 3 and 12 months in GH-treated boys and to identify key predictors of IGF-1 dynamics using interpretable modeling approaches.
METHODS: Data from 72 boys with growth hormone deficiency or idiopathic short stature from a previous Swedish clinical trial were analyzed using early-life characteristics, GH treatment variables, and puberty-related measures. Linear regression, Elastic Net regression, and explainable boosting machine (EBM) models were evaluated with nested five-fold patient-grouped cross-validation. Performance estimates were patient-balanced, with 95% confidence intervals based on 2,000 patient-cluster bootstrap resamples.
RESULTS: Elastic Net had the highest point estimates at 3 months, but confidence intervals did not establish a difference between the primary models. No clear differences between models were found at 12 months. Current IGF-1 SDS was the most prominent predictive feature, while additional treatment- and puberty-related variables were also selected across cross-validation models.
CONCLUSION: Interpretable modeling approaches provided moderate predictive performance for future IGF-1 SDS during the maintenance phase and puberty. The findings indicate that prediction is informed by current IGF-1 SDS together with additional clinical variables, but further validation in independent cohorts is required before clinical application.

title: Early post-weaning probiotic supplementation alters gut microbial community structure and predicted metabolic function in female juvenile mice.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To characterize the effects of early post-weaning multi-strain probiotic supplementation on gut microbiota composition, predicted metabolic function, and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) profiles in female juvenile mice at the pubertal window.
METHODS: Female C57BL/6 mice were randomly assigned to probiotic (Pro) or control (Con) groups; after gavage-related losses, final sample sizes were Pro: n = 9 and Con: n = 6. The probiotic suspension contained Bifidobacterium longum, Lactobacillus bulgaricus, and Streptococcus thermophilus and was administered from postnatal day 21 to 27. Fecal samples were collected during the three days preceding vaginal opening for 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V3-V4 region, DADA2/ASV pipeline, SILVA 138.1 database), PICRUSt2 functional prediction, and targeted SCFA quantification. PERMANOVA with multivariate dispersion testing was used for beta-diversity analysis, and Benjamini-Hochberg correction was applied for multiple comparisons.
RESULTS: A total of 2,946 ASVs were identified from 15 fecal samples. Probiotic supplementation significantly decreased alpha diversity (Observed species, Chao1, ACE, and Shannon; all P < 0.05) and altered overall community structure (PERMANOVA: Bray-Curtis R² = 0.193, P = 0.013; Jaccard R² = 0.158, P = 0.008), with no difference in multivariate dispersion. No genus remained significant after FDR correction. At a nominally significant level, Prevotellaceae UCG-001 and an unclassified Bacteroidales genus were depleted, while Dubosiella, Parabacteroides, and an unclassified Lachnospiraceae genus were enriched. Akkermansia showed a trend toward enrichment (9.39% vs. 45.85%; ANCOM-BC2: log2FC = +2.15, P = 0.179, FDR = 0.395). PICRUSt2 identified 63 MetaCyc pathways at nominal significance, none surviving FDR correction (minimum FDR = 0.106). SCFA analysis revealed nominally significant reductions in caproic acid (P = 0.039) and elevations in acetic acid (P = 0.039), neither surviving FDR correction (FDR = 0.121). Two correlations remained significant at the exploratory FDR < 0.1 threshold: Prevotellaceae UCG-001-acetic acid (rho = -0.693) and Akkermansia-valeric acid (rho = -0.670).
CONCLUSION: A brief post-weaning probiotic intervention significantly altered overall gut microbial community structure in female juvenile mice, with exploratory shifts in predicted functional capacity and a trend toward Akkermansia enrichment, without disrupting normal pubertal development. These findings should be considered exploratory given the small sample size.

title: Case Report: Intracranial germ cell tumors in girls presenting with peripheral precocious puberty and arginine vasopressin deficiency.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This report summarizes the clinical characteristics of three female children with clinically diagnosed β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG)-secreting intracranial germ cell tumors (iGCTs) who presented with peripheral precocious puberty (PPP) and arginine vasopressin deficiency (AVP-D), with the aim of facilitating earlier diagnosis and treatment.
METHODS: Clinical data of the 3 female patients with iGCTs with initial symptoms of PPP and AVP-D were retrospectively analyzed, and the relevant literature was reviewed.
RESULTS: All the 3 female children first had polydipsia and polyuria, but their parents paid no attention or sought no medical help until the girls developed thelarche. The children were diagnosed with PPP and AVP-D. Moreover, their β-hCG levels were elevated in the peripheral blood (PB) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and pituitary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed space-occupying lesions in the sellar region. Initial serum β-hCG concentrations in the 3 children were 5010.0, 314.3, and 202.8 mIU/mL, respectively. After regular chemotherapy and radiotherapy, β-hCG levels in the PB and CSF returned to normal, MRI scans revealed tumor reduction, Tanner stages regressed to stage I, and estradiol and testosterone levels decreased. Seven months after the treatment was completed, Patient 1 developed rapidly progressive central precocious puberty.
CONCLUSION: In children of either sex presenting with precocious puberty accompanied by multiple pituitary dysfunctions, including AVP-D, or mass effect manifestations, such as decreased visual acuity, routine serum β-hCG and AFP testing and contrast-enhanced sellar MRI are recommended to exclude organic lesions, including iGCTs.

title: Association between the triacylglycerol-glucose index, TyG-BMI and hypertension in children and adolescents: a cross-sectional study with machine-learning-based risk stratification.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension in children and adolescents is closely linked to obesity and metabolic disturbance. The triacylglycerol-glucose (TyG) index and TyG-BMI are surrogate markers of insulin resistance, but their associations with pediatric hypertension remain incompletely characterized.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 25,886 children and adolescents aged 7-17 years from 18 prefecture-level cities in Henan Province, China. The TyG index was calculated as ln[triglycerides (mg/dL) × fasting plasma glucose (mg/dL)/2] and TyG-BMI as TyG × BMI. Hypertension was defined as a blood pressure at or above the 95th percentile for age, sex and height (mean of the last two of three measurements). Logistic regression (Models I-IV) estimated odds ratios (ORs) per 1 SD and across quartiles, with non-linearity and effect modification assessed on both scales. Eleven machine-learning models were developed on a stratified 70:30 split, with imputation and feature selection performed strictly within the training set and discrimination (area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve, AUC) evaluated in the held-out validation set.
RESULTS: Among 25,886 participants, 1,798 (6.95%) had hypertension. Median TyG was 8.05 (IQR 7.77-8.35) and median TyG-BMI 154 (IQR 133-180). Each 1-SD increment in TyG was associated with hypertension in all models (Model IV 1.306 (95% CI 1.145-1.489)), and the association was graded across quartiles; TyG-BMI showed stronger associations (Model IV 2.109 (95% CI 1.985-2.241)). No multiplicative product term was significant after correction, whereas on the additive scale all six relative excess risk estimates were positive with confidence intervals excluding zero. In the held-out validation set, discrimination was moderate (best AUC 0.7544, 95% CI 0.7302-0.7777, for TyG and 0.7534, 0.7298-0.7759, for TyG-BMI), and adding either index to the same baseline model already containing BMI increased discrimination only marginally (about 0.003 in AUC).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher TyG and TyG-BMI were associated with hypertension in Chinese children and adolescents, more strongly for TyG-BMI. No multiplicative interaction survived correction, but all additive-scale estimates were positive, so effect modification cannot be excluded. Machine-learning models built from routinely available variables showed only moderate discrimination and remain hypothesis-generating tools for risk stratification rather than validated prediction models. Longitudinal studies are needed to assess causality.

title: Pregnancy in a Woman with PGM1-CDG: Longitudinal Metabolic Follow-up During a Lactose-Supported Diet.
abstract: Phosphoglucomutase-1 deficiency (PGM1-CDG) is an ultra-rare, treatable congenital disorder of glycosylation characterized by multisystem involvement. Although galactose supplementation improves biochemical and clinical manifestations, data on pregnancy management and metabolic follow-up in affected women remain extremely limited. We report a woman with genetically confirmed PGM1-CDG who achieved a successful pregnancy with detailed longitudinal metabolic monitoring and maintenance of galactose intake through a lactose-supported diet. The patient was diagnosed during adolescence with a multisystem phenotype including short stature, craniofacial dysmorphism, hepatic involvement, elevated creatine kinase, reduced antithrombin III and left ventricular hypertrophy. She harbored a homozygous PGM1 c.1508G>A (p.Arg503Gln) variant. Long-term pharmaceutical D-galactose supplementation was associated with biochemical improvement, while cardiac involvement remained clinically stable. At 25 years of age, pregnancy was achieved through assisted reproductive technology with her spouse, who was heterozygous for a different PGM1 variant classified as a variant of uncertain significance (VUS). Given the limited safety data on pharmaceutical D-galactose use during pregnancy and uncertainty regarding potential fetal effects, galactose intake was maintained through a lactose-supported diet (estimated galactose intake of approximately 0.5 g/kg/day). Liver enzymes, coagulation parameters and cardiac status remained stable and creatine kinase levels did not worsen. Gestational diabetes was successfully managed with dietary modification alone. No thrombotic, hepatic or cardiac complications occurred. A healthy female infant was delivered by elective cesarean section at 38 weeks. The newborn had a normal metabolic evaluation and was a heterozygous carrier of the maternal PGM1 variant. This case provides detailed longitudinal data on pregnancy in PGM1-CDG and describes the maintenance of dietary galactose intake derived from lactose during a pregnancy with favorable maternal and neonatal outcomes.

journal.title: Journal of clinical research in pediatric endocrinology

title: Longitudinal Changes in Exocrine Biomarkers in Children at Risk of Type 1 Diabetes in the ENDIA Study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The exocrine pancreas is increasingly implicated in type 1 diabetes. Noninvasive biomarkers of exocrine function, fecal elastase-1 (FE-1) and serum immunoreactive trypsin (IRT), may provide early insight into disease pathogenesis. We investigated the temporal relationship between exocrine biomarkers and type 1 diabetes development in children.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: FE-1 and IRT concentrations were measured prospectively in 301 at-risk children followed in the Environmental Determinants of Islet Autoimmunity (ENDIA) cohort from birth. A total of 216 children provided 1,679 stool samples; 242 provided 1,014 serum samples. Biomarker trajectories were compared between children who developed islet autoimmunity or type 1 diabetes and age- and sex-matched control children negative for autoantibodies in a nested case-control design. Adjusted linear mixed models were used.
RESULTS: Two biomarker patterns were observed. FE-1 concentrations were lower during the first 6 months of life in children who subsequently developed multiple islet autoantibodies or type 1 diabetes (β-coefficient at birth -0.61 [95% CI -1.04, -0.17]; P = 0.006; β-coefficient at 3 months -0.39 [95% CI -0.69, -0.09]; P = 0.010); IRT concentrations were lower in children who developed type 1 diabetes 12 months (β = -0.30 [95% CI -0.58, -0.02]; P = 0.034) and 18 months (β = -0.40 [95% CI -0.71, -0.10]; P = 0.008) before type 1 diabetes diagnosis.
CONCLUSIONS: Changes in exocrine biomarkers were detectable early in the natural history of type 1 diabetes, with a delayed rise of FE-1 in infants who later progressed to multiple islet autoantibodies or type 1 diabetes and a decrease in IRT following islet autoantibody seroconversion.

title: The 2024 National Report on Continuous Glucose Monitoring Uptake in Pediatric Type 1 Diabetes Following Universal Funding in Aotearoa New Zealand: Early Findings from the KiwiDiab Pediatric Diabetes Network.
abstract:
AIM: To describe national patterns in continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) uptake and glycemic patterns among children with type 1 diabetes (T1D) in Aotearoa New Zealand following universal CGM funding on October 1, 2024.
METHODS: Data from the KiwiDiab pediatric diabetes network for 2024 included children <16 years with T1D who were attending 14 regional pediatric diabetes centers. CGM uptake was evaluated using the weekly proportion using CGM and the weekly proportion initiating CGM. Overall and ethnicity-specific initiation was analyzed using negative binomial regression of weekly initiation counts, with the number not using CGM at the start of each week as an offset, comparing prefunding, rollout, and postfunding periods. HbA1c measurements were summarized as cross-sectional monthly distributions by prioritized ethnicity.
RESULTS: In total, 1681 children and adolescents with T1D were included. Mean weekly proportions initiating CGM increased from 1.4% prefunding to 12.9% during rollout (incidence rate ratio [IRR] = 9.05, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.03-17.5) and remained elevated postfunding at 6.6% (IRR = 4.64, 95% CI: 3.27-6.61). During rollout, mean weekly proportions initiating CGM increased from 1.0% to 14.0% among Māori, from 0.8% to 11.6% among Pacific, from 1.5% to 15.9% among Asian, and from 1.8% to 11.0% among European children. There was no statistically significant evidence that the magnitude of change across funding periods differed by ethnicity (period-by-ethnicity interaction, P = 0.72). Differences in the proportion using CGM between ethnic groups narrowed during 2024 but remained at year-end. Cross-sectional HbA1c distributions remained relatively stable throughout 2024, with no clear early lowering observed.
CONCLUSION: Universal CGM funding was associated with a rapid increase in CGM uptake across Aotearoa New Zealand. CGM initiation increased markedly across ethnic groups, and ethnic disparities in CGM use narrowed during 2024, although they persisted at year-end.

title: Sellar spine in children and young adults: clinical presentation, imaging characteristics, and pituitary outcomes.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The true clinical relevance of a sellar spine remains unclear because of limited available data. We aimed to describe the presentation and associated pituitary dysfunction among children and young adults with a sellar spine.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients with a sellar spine found on brain imaging obtained in individuals less than 25 years of age. Extracted variables included age at initial brain imaging, indication for imaging, and pituitary dysfunction status and type.
RESULTS: Eleven patients were included. Age at initial identification of a sellar spine ranged from 6 to 24 years. Indications for neuroimaging included headaches (n=3), seizures (n=2), precocious puberty (n=1), severe obesity with advanced bone age (n=1), suspected stroke/ataxia (n=1), nasal polyp evaluation (n=1), hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and secondary hypothyroidism (n=1), and as part of screening testing for Von Hipple Lindau (n=1). Pituitary stalk deviation was found in 7 patients (63.6 %). Pituitary gland distorted morphology leading to a misdiagnosis of pituitary adenoma found in 2 patients (18.2 %). Among younger children (n=5; age ≤9 years), precocious puberty occurred in one patient who demonstrated pituitary stalk deviation with an AP size-to-sella ratio of 0.5. Another child with stalk deviation did not develop precocious puberty. Pituitary hormone deficiency was identified in one patient (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and hypothyroidism) with stalk deviation and AP size-to-sella ratio of 0.63.
CONCLUSIONS: The presence of a sellar spine can distort pituitary anatomy and result in diagnostic misclassification. Endocrinopathies may develop in some affected patients. Further, larger studies are warranted to better define the characteristics of sellar spine leading to endocrinopathies.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Longitudinal changes in bone mineral density, bone turnover markers, and body composition in children and adolescents treated for acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Impaired bone mineral density (BMD) is a common finding in young patients with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). Nevertheless, longitudinal trendlines of BMD and the impact of body composition (BC) on bone health still need to be explored among pediatric survivors. The objective of the study is to report longitudinal changes in BMD and BC in pediatric patients.
METHODS: This prospective, longitudinal study, collecting BMD and BC (assessed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry [DXA]) and circulating bone turnover markers every 6 months for 3 years, from diagnosis of ALL (T0) until 1 year after the end of antiblastic treatment (T6).
RESULTS: Forty-nine patients were enrolled. At T0, lumbar spine (LS-)BMD Z-score was ≤-2.0 in 71.7% of patients [median: -2.8 (-3.5, -1.9)], possibly reflecting trabecular bone infiltration by lymphoblasts. Conversely, total body less than head (TBLH)-BMD Z-score was >-2.0 in 97.8% of patients at T0 but abruptly declined after 6 months (p < 0.001). Despite a recovery trend after the end of treatment, LS or TBLH-BMD Z-scores were still <-2.0 in 67.7% of the 31 patients still enrolled at T6. Bone turnover was increased between T1 and T4. Lean mass decreased over time, while fat mass progressively increased. Multivariable analysis showed a statistically significant association between appendicular lean mass longitudinal recovery over time and T1-T6 TBLH-BMD trendlines (p = 0.008).
CONCLUSIONS: In pediatric patients, LS-BMD is remarkably affected at diagnosis of ALL. TBLH-BMD, normal at diagnosis, promptly declines during treatment and baseline values are not retrieved after 36 months. Lean mass is positively associated with longitudinal improvements of subtotal BMD over time.

title: The lost scent of excitation: dissociation between cognitive desire and physical arousal in Kallmann syndrome.
abstract: Kallmann syndrome (KS) is a rare form of congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (CHH) that causes delayed puberty and infertility, accompanied by a lifelong loss of smell. While hormone replacement therapy (HRT) restores standard hormone levels, the specific impact of an absent sense of smell on sexual relationships and desire remains largely unstudied. This study examined how lifelong smell loss shapes the psychosexual experiences of affected individuals. 38 adults were evaluated: 19 patients receiving stable HRT (10 with KS who lacked a sense of smell and 9 with CHH but normal smell) and 19 healthy matched individuals. Participants completed validated questionnaires assessing sexual desire, physical arousal, romantic behaviors, and attitudes toward intimacy. HRT effectively restored baseline sexual desire and general attitudes across all patients. However, individuals with KS reported significantly lower physical sexual arousal and engaged in far fewer sexual behaviors than those with an intact sense of smell. The lack of smell independently predicted lower arousal levels, despite patients maintaining normal mental desire and positive attitudes toward sex. These findings show that hormone therapy alone is insufficient to fully restore the sexual experience in KS. The lifelong absence of smell creates a distinct divide between mental desire and physical arousal, undermining sexual confidence and intimacy. Healthcare providers should therefore incorporate psychosexual counseling into routine clinical care to help patients navigate these sensory and emotional challenges.

title: Temple syndrome in Chinese children: a case series and literature review.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Temple syndrome (TS14) is a rare imprinting disorder caused by aberrations at chromosome 14q32, manifesting as pre- and postnatal growth retardation, delayed motor milestones, and central precocious puberty (CPP). No cohort studies have characterized TS14 in Chinese children.
METHODS: Six patients from two tertiary hospitals in China were included in this study. All patients underwent molecular testing using whole exome sequencing (WES) and methylation-specific multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MS-MLPA). Their clinical and molecular characteristics were systematically described. Two patients received recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) therapy, one of whom was treated with long-acting GH. In addition, a structured literature review of TS14 was performed.
RESULTS: Six patients, all born small for gestational age and exhibiting persistent postnatal growth retardation, were molecularly diagnosed with TS14. In Patient 3, negative WES findings combined with an abnormal MS-MLPA result supported a methylation abnormality as the underlying mechanism. Patient 1 presented with CPP, and patient 3 with rapidly progressive early puberty, whereas patients 4-6 harbored additional molecular findings, including a de novo DYNC1H1 deletion, a YY1-region deletion, and a homozygous GALC c.1901T>C variant; the findings in patients 4 and 5 may have contributed to blended phenotypes. In patient 1, combined gonadotropin-releasing hormone analog (GnRHa) and rhGH therapy resulted in a height gain of +1.0 standard deviation scores (SDS) over 1.5 years, while patient 3, who received long-acting GH, achieved a height gain of +1.74 SDS over 2.5 years. A review of 167 TS14 cases showed broadly similar core clinical features across ethnicities, although Asian patients exhibited lower rates of facial dysmorphism and obesity. Additional molecular findings, including multilocus imprinting abnormalities and potential blended phenotypes, were also identified in reported cases. Adult heights as low as -3.3 SDS were reported in untreated patients, whereas rhGH ± GnRHa improved growth outcomes but did not consistently normalize adult height.
CONCLUSION: This series broadens the clinical characterization of TS14 in Chinese children and highlights the diagnostic value of comprehensive molecular testing, particularly in patients with atypical features. Hormonal treatment may improve growth velocity in selected patients, but long-term benefits, final height outcomes and optimal timing remain uncertain.

title: Perspectives and experiences of youth and caregivers on screening and monitoring islet autoimmunity.
abstract:
AIMS: Screening and monitoring programs for islet autoantibodies, which signal risk of clinical type 1 diabetes, are being implemented globally. No studies have qualitatively explored youths' perspectives on islet autoimmunity screening and monitoring, nor integrated their views with those of caregivers.
METHODS: We interviewed 35 Australian youth (aged 9-18 years; median age = 11.5 years; n = 18 girls) with one or more islet autoantibodies and 49 caregivers of affected youth. Youth had been monitored for approximately 9 years (median). All families, except one, had a relative with type 1 diabetes. Twenty-one (42.86%) caregivers lived with clinical type 1 diabetes. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis.
RESULTS: Seven themes reflected our findings. Youth had limited understanding of the advantages of monitoring outside of research. They were predominantly focused on testing experiences rather than clinical risk. Caregivers generally displayed strong psychological responses, as did older adolescents. Family experience of diabetes shaped psychological responses in multifaceted ways. Caregivers further emphasised flexible service delivery and specific logistical considerations for screening and monitoring.
CONCLUSIONS: Youths' focus on the practicalities of testing, rather than health risk, is reassuring in the context of planning international screening and monitoring programs. However, it highlights the need to prioritise procedural experiences. Youth should also be educated on the real-world benefits of monitoring. Psychosocial support is needed, particularly for caregivers and older adolescents, with healthcare individualised to the unique influence of family history of clinical diabetes. Caregivers further need reliable, structured monitoring pathways to manage distress, with equity and accessibility prioritised for sustained engagement.

title: Effectiveness of a physical literacy intervention program for young and middle-aged adults with hypertension: a mixed-methods quasi-experimental study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To examine whether a theoretically grounded, 8-week physical literacy intervention incorporating salutogenic model components (sense of coherence, social support, and self-efficacy) could improve physical activity levels and clinical outcomes in young and middle-aged adults with Grade 1 hypertension, and to explore participants' subjective experiences of the program.
METHODS: A mixed-methods quasi-experimental study was conducted between August and October 2024. Forty patients aged 18-59 years were recruited from a community healthcare center and allocated to the intervention group (n = 20) or control group (n = 20). The intervention group received a multidimensional physical-literacy program, while the control group received usual care. Five participants were lost to follow-up; 35 (intervention: n = 17; control: n = 18) completed all three assessments: baseline (T0), post-intervention (T1), and one-month follow-up (T2). Quantitative outcomes (SBP, BMI, physical-literacy scores, social support, sense of coherence, self-efficacy, and physical activity) were analyzed using independent t-tests or Mann-Whitney U tests for between-group comparisons and paired t-tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for within-group changes, with significance set at α = 0.05 (two-tailed). Qualitative data from semi-structured interviews were analyzed using inductive content analysis.
RESULTS: Of the 40 recruited participants, 35 (87.5%) completed the study. Post-intervention, the intervention group demonstrated significant reductions in systolic blood pressure (SBP), body weight, and BMI compared to baseline (all P < 0.05). Significant improvements were also observed in PL scores, social support, sense of coherence, and self-efficacy (P < 0.05). Qualitative findings corroborated these results, highlighting enhanced health literacy and stress alleviation, despite some logistical challenges.
CONCLUSION: The PL intervention is a feasible and effective strategy to improve health outcomes and psychosocial resilience in hypertensive adults, offering a promising approach for community-based chronic disease management.

title: Clinical characteristics of paediatric-onset type 2 diabetes: a comparison by weight status in the Hong Kong childhood diabetes registry 2008 to 2023.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Although obesity is a major risk factor for paediatric type 2 diabetes (T2DM), many Asian youths present without obesity. This phenotype remains under-recognised and poorly described. This study aimed to compare the clinical and metabolic characteristics of children newly diagnosed with T2DM, stratified by weight status, in Hong Kong.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study using data from the Hong Kong Childhood Diabetes Registry (2008-2023). We compared the clinical and metabolic features of children with and without obesity who were newly diagnosed with T2DM.
RESULTS: A total of 689 children (96 % Chinese) were included and 35 % were children without obesity. While age at diagnosis was similar between groups, children without obesity exhibited a higher prevalence of family history of T2DM (80.6 % vs. 67.5 %; p<0.0001), more frequent presentations of classical symptoms and diabetic ketoacidosis with or without hyperosmolar hyperglycaemia state (4.6 % vs. 1.6 %, p=0.0262), and higher HbA1c and blood glucose levels at diagnosis, with lower HOMA-%B, suggesting greater β-cell dysfunction. Conversely children with obesity had higher insulin resistance. They also had higher prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), hypertension, hyperuricaemia, obstructive sleep apnoea, and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Insulin therapy was more frequently required at diagnosis in children without obesity (16.3 % vs. 8 %, p=0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: These results highlight a distinct T2DM phenotype in Chinese children without obesity, marked by severe hyperglycaemia and a higher rate of insulin requirement at diagnosis. Increased clinical vigilance for this under-recognised group is warranted to optimise management at diagnosis, with long term outcomes to be address in future longitudinal studies.

journal.title: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Case Report: Neurosurgery, octreotide, cabergoline, radiotherapy, pasireotide and pegvisomant - a multimodal strategy for adolescent acrogigantism.
abstract: Growth hormone (GH)-secreting pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) are rare in the pediatric population. They often present as large, invasive tumors and are frequently associated with an underlying genetic predisposition, making their management particularly challenging. Optimal treatment requires an individualized multidisciplinary approach, which often involves a combination of surgery and adjuvant medical therapy or radiotherapy when necessary. We present a challenging case of an adolescent female with acrogigantism. The patient was diagnosed at the age of 13 years and 10 months during the evaluation of chronic headaches. Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed an invasive PitNET measuring 38 × 23 × 32 mm, while biochemical assessment confirmed marked GH hypersecretion. The disease followed an aggressive course, and biochemical control could not be achieved despite optimal multimodal therapy. Sequential treatment included neurosurgical resection, octreotide LAR, cabergoline, pasireotide LAR, proton beam radiotherapy, and pegvisomant. Combination therapy with pegvisomant and octreotide LAR ultimately normalized insulin-like growth factor 1 concentrations while maintaining long-term radiological tumor stability. This case underscores the complexity of managing aggressive GH-secreting PitNETs in adolescents and emphasizes the need for individualized, multidisciplinary care and long-term follow-up. Combined medical therapy with pegvisomant and octreotide LAR may provide effective biochemical control when surgery, radiotherapy, and standard medical treatment are insufficient.

title: Parent experiences of infant feeding in congenital hyperinsulinism: a thematic analysis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Congenital Hyperinsulinism (CHI) is a rare condition of hypoglycaemia due to excess insulin secretion. Feeding problems are frequent, and often persistent, in patients with CHI. The range, extent and persistence of feeding problems has been described, but parent and family perspectives are lacking. As feeding is a key aspect of the maintenance of glycaemic stability, and a vital part of infant development and family bonding, it is important to understand the impact of feeding problems on parents and caregivers. This qualitative study explored caregivers' experiences of feeding during the initial years following diagnosis.
METHODS: We conducted semi-structured interviews with caregivers of patients with CHI, from a single international centre of excellence. Patients had received a confirmed genetic diagnosis of CHI between 2015 and 2025. All interviews were completed using Microsoft Teams, recorded and transcribed. Transcriptions were analysed using thematic analysis to identify themes.
RESULTS: Thematic analysis identified four main themes; Theme 1: Medical Management Disrupts Feeding: Frequent feeding schedules, enteral tube feeding and medication regimens were perceived to interfere with the establishment of typical feeding behaviours and family mealtime routines. Theme 2: Feeding Aversion and Delayed Oral Development: Parents described feeding aversion and delays in oral feeding skill development, with many children demonstrating reduced interest in eating, reluctance to try new foods and prolonged dependence on enteral feeding. Theme 3: Feeding Driven by Glycaemic Control: Feeding was consistently described as being targeted to maintain glycaemic stability rather than respond to hunger and satiety cues. Theme 4: Psychosocial Impact on Families: Feeding challenges had a substantial psychosocial impact on families, contributing to parental stress and anxiety, increasing caregiver burden, and affecting family routines, social activities and confidence around mealtimes.
CONCLUSION: This study identified the complex, demanding and distressing challenges faced by families of infants with CHI, adversely affecting family wellbeing. Early multidisciplinary input, including dietetics, speech and language therapy, and psychological support, along with practical CHI-specific feeding guidance may reduce burden and improve outcomes. The findings of this study highlight the need for training and education in local healthcare teams managing CHI.

title: Causes of discordance between noninvasive prenatal testing and fetal chromosomal status: a 10-year cohort study of 97, 743 cases.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Noninvasive prenatal testing (NIPT) has been widely adopted for screening common fetal chromosomal aneuploidies, yet discordance between NIPT results and true fetal karyotypes remains a critical challenge limiting its clinical utility.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 97, 743 pregnant women who underwent NIPT at Ganzhou Women and Children's Health Care Hospital between April 2015 and December 2024 to evaluate the performance of NIPT and investigate the causes of discordance between NIPT results and fetal outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 481 NIPT-positive cases were identified, yielding an overall positive rate of 0.49%. Of these, 380 cases underwent confirmatory testing (377 via invasive prenatal diagnosis and 3 via postnatal karyotyping). The overall positive predictive value (PPV) for the three common trisomies was 71.84%, with T21 showing the highest PPV (84.38%), followed by T18 (56.00%) and T13 (4.76%). Stratified analysis by Z-score demonstrated that PPVs for both T21 and T18 increased progressively with higher Z-score. For T21, PPV rose from 21.95% (Z: 3-6) to 100% (Z > 20); a similar upward trend was observed for T18. False-positive results were attributed to multiple mechanisms, including maternal chromosomal abnormalities (4 full 47, XX, + 21, 1 mosaic), vanishing twin (7 cases), uniparental disomy (2 cases), and confined placental mosaicism (CPM) (2 cases). Only 3 false-negative cases were identified, predominantly due to low-level placental mosaicism.
CONCLUSIONS: Discordance between NIPT and fetal karyotype exhibits a clear directional divergence: false-positive results are etiologically heterogeneous, involving maternal chromosomal abnormalities, substantially underestimated vanishing twin, CPM, and technical factors, whereas false-negative results are predominantly attributable to low-level CPM. Systematic analysis of Z-scores, maternal characteristics, and follow-up data can effectively identify most discordance causes, providing precise evidence for genetic counseling and pregnancy management. Our analytical framework provides a practical reference for optimizing NIPT screening strategies and reducing unnecessary invasive procedures in other regions.

title: Association of baseline body mass index with growth responses to growth hormone therapy in children with growth hormone deficiency.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the association of baseline body mass index (BMI) status with long-term growth and metabolic outcomes during growth hormone (GH) therapy in children with GH deficiency (GHD).
METHODS: From the LG Growth Study, we analyzed 155 children with GHD receiving GH for ≥36 months after age-based propensity score matching (78 elevated-BMI; 77 normal-BMI). Multivariable regression assessed baseline BMI-standard deviation score (SDS) in relation to 36-month changes in height SDS by bone age (BA). Group comparisons assessed longitudinal growth and metabolic outcomes; separate matched obesity and overweight analyses were exploratory.
RESULTS: Baseline height SDS by chronological age (CA) did not differ significantly between groups (-2.33 ± 0.58 vs. -2.45 ± 0.65; p=0.1464), whereas height SDS by BA was higher in the elevated-BMI group (0.00 ± 1.68 vs. -0.73 ± 1.28; p=0.0131). Height velocity trajectories were similar (group-by-time p=0.9585). Height SDS by CA improved comparably between groups, whereas ΔHeight SDS by BA differed significantly at 12 months (p=0.0387) and 36 months (p=0.001). Higher baseline BMI-SDS was associated with a lower 36-month change in height SDS by BA in the adjusted model (β=-0.3525; p=0.0216). BMI-SDS decreased in the elevated-BMI group during the first year (p<0.0001), and total cholesterol decreased in both groups.
CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline BMI-SDS was associated with a lower 36-month change in height SDS by BA during GH therapy, while CA-based height gains did not differ significantly between groups.

title: Distinct phenotypes associated with the same homozygous ENPP1 c.26dup variant.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: ENPP1 pathogenic variants have been associated with a wide phenotypic spectrum, ranging from generalized arterial calcification of infancy to vascular stenoses and autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets.
CASE PRESENTATION: This study presents two cases of cousins who are homozygous for the c.26dup (p.Gly10ArgfsTer67) variant in the ENPP1 gene, but who exhibit distinct clinical features. The first patient developed hypophosphatemic rickets in early childhood. He was subsequently diagnosed with hypertension due to multiple arterial stenoses. In the second case, prenatal monitoring revealed generalized vascular calcification of intrauterine onset. Postnatally, the patient was diagnosed with heart failure, for which medical therapy was initiated, and early parenteral pamidronate was administered. However, the infant died during infancy due to a respiratory infection.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that ENPP1 variants may manifest with heterogeneous phenotypes and modifying factors may influence the variant's clinical expression. Case 1 was previously reported with limited clinical information as part of a national Turkish cohort of patients with autosomal recessive hypophosphatemic rickets type 2 caused by ENPP1 deficiency. However, as the study was a cohort analysis, it did not comprehensively describe the patient's clinical course, cardiovascular involvement, long-term follow-up, or the intrafamilial phenotypic variability observed within the affected family. Our report contributes to a better understanding of this rare genetic disorder's clinical spectrum and to clarifying the genotype-phenotype correlation.

title: Clinical manifestations of resistance to thyroid hormone beta (RTHβ) syndrome in children - multicenter case series.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Resistance to thyroid hormone (TH) β (RTHβ) is a rare genetic disorder caused by mutations in the TH receptor β gene (THRB) and characterized by elevated TH levels with non-suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and variable clinical presentation. The aim of the study was to characterize the clinical and biochemical features of children with RTHβ, correlate them with genetic findings and therapeutic management, to raise clinicians' awareness of the specific characteristics of the condition.
MATERIAL AND METHODS: This retrospective multicenter case series included 15 children with genetically confirmed THRB variants. Clinical, laboratory, imaging, and treatment data were analyzed retrospectively.
RESULTS: All the patients demonstrated elevated free thyroxine and free triiodothyronine concentrations with detectable, non-suppressed TSH serum level. Common findings included tachycardia (73%), neurodevelopmental disturbances (60%), and a lean phenotype (BMI <10th percentile, 53%). Misdiagnosis of primary hyperthyroidism occurred in 20% of cases. Most patients did not require pharmacological treatment or were managed with beta-blockers alone for symptomatic tachycardia control.
DISCUSSION: Pediatric RTHβ shows consistent biochemical features but marked clinical heterogeneity. Awareness is essential to ensure accurate diagnosis and avoid unnecessary therapy.

title: Serum Vitamin D Status and Bone Accrual Trajectories in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis: A 6-Year Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: In adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS), low bone mineral density (BMD) and impaired bone qualities have been demonstrated to be an important risk factor for curve progression. This prospective cohort study evaluated associations of repeated serum 25OHD measurements with BMD and volumetric bone qualities from early adolescence to early adulthood in AIS patients with low BMD.
METHODS: A total of 110 girls with AIS (aged 11-14 years, femoral neck BMD Z-score ≤ 0) were recruited (baseline) and followed up at 1, 2, and 6 years thereafter. Longitudinal data of bone parameters and serum 25OHD were analyzed using linear mixed-effect models. Patients were categorized into persistent severe Vitamin D (Vit-D) deficiency (≥ 2 measurements of 25OHD < 30 nmol/L), persistent Vit-D deficiency (≥ 2 measurements of 25OHD < 50 nmol/L), or normal groups. Difference between Vit-D status was compared using ANCOVA.
RESULTS: Patients were followed from a mean age of 12.98 ± 0.85 to 19.25 ± 0.90 years. During the peripubertal period (from baseline to 2-year follow-up), higher 25OHD levels were shown to be associated with higher total volumetric BMD (0.22 mg/cm3 per unit of 25OHD (adjusted), p = 0.043). At early adulthood (6-year follow-up), persistent severe Vit-D deficiency group exhibited lower total volumetric BMD (353.55 ± 45.67 vs 398.36 ± 66.65 mg/cm3, p = 0.018), lower cortical volumetric BMD (904.59 ± 31.05 vs 922.371 ± 21.29 mg/cm3, p = 0.033), and less cortical thickness (0.92 ± 0.13 vs 1.02 ± 0.12 mm, p = 0.024).
CONCLUSION: Low 25OHD is associated with suboptimal BMD and impaired volumetric bone qualities during the peripubertal period in adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis. Persistent severe Vit-D deficiency predicts poor early adulthood bone outcomes, supporting future evaluation of interventional strategies.

title: Biphasic neonatal Graves disease following maternal thyroidectomy: a case report.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To describe transient neonatal hyperthyroidism in a preterm infant born to a mother with Graves disease previously treated by total thyroidectomy, with no antenatal TRAb assessment and a postpartum maternal TRAb result documented as negative.
CASE PRESENTATION: A male infant was born at 33+6 weeks' gestation to a mother with Graves disease and orbitopathy who had undergone total thyroidectomy 5 years earlier and was receiving levothyroxine. Maternal TRAb were not measured during pregnancy. A privately performed postpartum thyrotropin receptor antibodies (TRAb) test was reviewed by the treating physicians and documented as negative, although the original laboratory report was unavailable. At birth, the infant had suppressed TSH, FT4 >6.28 ng/dL, FT3 22.48 pg/mL, and TRAb 60 IU/L. Thyroid hormone concentrations initially declined spontaneously, with TRAb decreasing to 31 IU/L by day 26. On day 33, FT4 and FT3 increased again, accompanied by agitation and episodic tachycardia. Methimazole was started on day 34. Thyroid function progressively improved, treatment was discontinued on day 110, and subsequent follow-up confirmed persistent euthyroidism.
CONCLUSIONS: Postpartum maternal TRAb results cannot retrospectively define fetal antibody exposure. This case also illustrates that neonatal Graves disease may show a biphasic biochemical course requiring serial monitoring.
