title: Pituitary volume as a permissive morphological threshold for hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis activation in children: a comprehensive diagnostic prediction study with relative importance decomposition.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) stimulation test, the reference standard for confirming hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis (HPGA) activation, is invasive and costly. Pituitary volume (PV) on MRI has been proposed as a non-invasive surrogate, yet whether PV constitutes a permissive morphological threshold or is redundant with clinical parameters remains undefined. We evaluated PV as a morphological threshold of HPGA activation and quantified its relative importance, unique information content, and clinical utility.
METHODS: We retrospectively enrolled 896 children who underwent pituitary MRI and GnRH stimulation testing. PV was measured using the ellipsoid approximation. Out-of-fold cross-validated AUC was the primary performance metric. Predictor importance was quantified by Shapley value decomposition, permutation importance, and Lindeman-Merenda-Gold (LMG) variance partitioning. Morphological-threshold analyses examined HPGA activation across PV deciles. Statistical mediation tested whether insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) mediated the PV-HPGA association, with formal power analysis for incremental AUC detection.
RESULTS: PV exhibited a threshold pattern: HPGA activation was 28.9% (95% CI 20.5-39.0) in the lowest PV decile (≤115 mm³) versus 92.2% (95% CI 84.8-96.2) in the highest (≥335 mm³; OR 4.38, 95% CI 2.60-7.36; per-IQR OR 2.04, 95% CI 1.59-2.62). PV ranked second by Shapley decomposition (+0.065 AUC, 22.2%), carrying unique information (LMG 20.4% of pseudo-R²). At the 203.9 mm³ cutpoint, the diagnostic odds ratio was 4.78, positive likelihood ratio 2.44, and number needed to screen 2.73. PV tertile AUC was 0.693; combined with IGF-1, AUC rose to 0.748. IGF-1 statistically mediated 37.4% of the PV-HPGA association. The full model OOF AUC was 0.801 (95% CI 0.772-0.828) versus 0.798 for the clinical model (ΔAUC +0.003); power was ~5% at N = 896, requiring N ≈ 25360 for 80% power. The age-sex-adjusted PV z-score AUC was 0.592 (95% CI 0.554-0.630).
CONCLUSION: PV serves as a permissive morphological threshold for HPGA activation; while it's not a strictly necessary condition, HPGA activation is physiologically improbable below a critical PV. Although PV is not a standalone predictive tool and its incremental value over clinical parameters is minimal, it functions as a complementary morphological checkpoint that contextualizes hormonal interpretation when pituitary MRI has been conducted to exclude intracranial lesions as per guidelines.

title: Pregnancy-associated alterations in circulating vitamin D metabolites: higher total 25-hydroxyvitamin D and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D without increased free 25-hydroxyvitamin D.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interpretation of vitamin D biomarkers during pregnancy remains challenging because physiological adaptations alter total and free vitamin D metabolites differently, while evidence comparing multiple circulating vitamin D metabolites within the same clinical setting remains limited.
METHODS: We conducted a large real-world laboratory-based cross-sectional study using routine clinical data from women aged 18-45 years tested at a German diagnostic center between 2014 and 2020. Total 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D], free 25-hydroxyvitamin D, and total 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D [1,25(OH)2D] concentrations were compared between pregnant and nonpregnant women and across gestation using age-adjusted regression models. Complementary random-effects meta-analyses were performed for free 25-hydroxyvitamin D and total 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D.
RESULTS: After exclusions, 101,454 nonpregnant and 16,017 pregnant women comprised the overall study population, with analyte-specific sample sizes reflecting availability in routine clinical practice. In age-adjusted analyses, pregnancy was associated with higher total 25(OH)D concentrations (adjusted difference 22.07 nmol/L; 95% CI, 21.50-22.63; P<0.001) and markedly higher total 1,25(OH)2D concentrations (adjusted difference 125.20 pmol/L; 95% CI, 115.39-135.02; P<0.001). Both metabolites were higher at later gestational stages in cross-sectional analyses. In contrast, directly measured free 25(OH)D did not differ significantly between pregnant and nonpregnant women (adjusted difference, -2.63 pmol/L; 95% CI, -8.99 to 3.74; P = 0.417). Complementary meta-analyses showed higher total 1,25(OH)2D and modestly lower free 25(OH)D concentrations during pregnancy; sensitivity analyses excluding the current cohort yielded similar overall patterns.
CONCLUSIONS: Pregnancy was associated with higher total 25(OH)D and markedly higher total 1,25(OH)2D. No statistically significant difference in free 25(OH)D was detected in the much smaller available subgroup; this finding should be considered exploratory and requires confirmation in larger studies. These results highlight the importance of analyte-specific interpretation of vitamin D biomarkers during pregnancy.

title: Sex differences in the prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in hospitalized patients: a single-center cross-sectional study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The influence of sex and age on the prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) among hospitalized patients remains unclear.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 136,816 hospitalized adults (2014-2023) at the People's Hospital of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region. Hepatic steatosis was confirmed by ultrasonography. Sex-specific prevalence was analyzed across younger (18-50 years) and older (51-80 years) age groups.
RESULTS: MASLD prevalence was 28.8% (39,431/136,816). MASLD patients were older than those without MASLD (median 58 vs. 53 years; P < 0.001). Within the hospitalized population, age-stratified analysis revealed sex-specific differences in the odds of MASLD reversal. Women aged 18-50 had a lower prevalence of MASLD than men (OR< 1, P < 0.001), whereas women aged 51-80 had a higher prevalence (OR> 1, P < 0.001). After adjustment for age, calendar year, and sex × age interaction, the sex difference remained significant (P < 0.001). Women aged 18-50 years had lower adjusted odds of MASLD than men (aOR = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.48-0.52), whereas women aged 51-80 years had higher adjusted odds (aOR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.64-1.74). Comparing older women (aged 51-80) with younger women (aged 18-50), the prevalence of MASLD was significantly higher among older women (P < 0.001). Among all patients, older hospitalized patients also exhibited more pronounced metabolic abnormalities, including elevated BMI (81.8% vs. 44.1%), elevated blood pressure (72.2% vs. 61.0%), and elevated triglycerides (44.6% vs. 20.8%) (all P < 0.001).
CONCLUSION: Early MASLD screening should be prioritized in hospitalized women aged 50 years and older and hospitalized men under 50 years, particularly those with metabolic prevalence factors, to enable timely intervention and reduce the development and progression of MASLD.

title: Case Report: GADA-positive type 1 diabetes with diabetic ketoacidosis in a young adult with obesity temporally associated with unsupervised tirzepatide use for weight reduction.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 (GIP/GLP-1) receptor agonist, is widely used as an anti-obesity medication. Its safety in individuals with unrecognized type 1 diabetes (T1D) remains uncertain.
CASE DESCRIPTION: We describe a 28-year-old man with obesity and no previously documented hyperglycemia who self-administered tirzepatide, lost 15 kg over about 3 months, and was later diagnosed with GADA-positive T1D presenting as diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) in temporal association with drug use and discontinuation. At admission, fasting blood glucose (FBG) was 13.99 mmol/L, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) 10.8% (95 mmol/mol), serum β-hydroxybutyrate 4.44 mmol/L, urine ketones (+++), serum bicarbonate 16.9 mmol/L, glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody (GADA) >2000 IU/mL, and fasting C-peptide 0.798 ng/mL. Admission arterial blood gas was not obtained. Insulin therapy was initiated; HbA1c was 6.7% (50 mmol/mol) at 3 months.
CONCLUSIONS: This single case cannot establish causality between tirzepatide exposure or discontinuation and autoimmune diabetes. It illustrates that adult-onset GADA-positive T1D with DKA may be recognized during or after unsupervised incretin-based weight reduction. Markedly elevated HbA1c indicated that hyperglycemia likely preceded the short symptomatic phase. The main clinical message is that autoimmune diabetes should be considered when unexplained hyperglycemia, ongoing weight loss, or ketoacidosis develops in this setting.

title: Long-acting growth hormone therapy in Chinese children with idiopathic short stature: efficacy evaluation and influencing factors.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Exogenous growth hormone (GH) supplementation is the primary strategy for treating idiopathic short stature (ISS). Although long-acting growth hormone (LAGH) has attracted considerable interest due to its reduced injection frequency, data on its comparative efficacy and long-term safety in Chinese children with ISS remain limited. This study aims to assess LAGH's efficacy in this population and identify the factors influencing therapeutic outcomes.
METHODS: This study was a single-center, retrospective cohort study. It included 180 ISS children who received LAGH treatment in our hospital from January 2019 to December 2024. Based on age, gender, and height standard deviation score (HtSDS), a 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) was conducted to select concurrent ISS patients receiving short-acting growth hormone (daily rhGH) treatment. Treatment efficacy was evaluated according to the changes in HtSDS and growth velocity (GV) before and after treatment, and multivariate regression analysis was used to identify factors influencing clinical efficacy.
RESULTS: The average age of children in the LAGH group was 8.37 ± 2.49 years. After treatment, the LAGH group showed significantly higher HtSDS (-1.47 ± 0.31 vs. -1.63 ± 0.48, p<0.001) and GV (10.06 ± 1.69 vs. 9.24 ± 1.34, p<0.001) compared to the control group for 12 months. Pearson correlation analysis revealed that IGF-1 most correlated with GV (r=0.58, p<0.001). Multivariate regression showed GH efficacy positively correlated with ΔIGF-1 (β=0.42, p<0.001) and IGFBP-3 (β=0.28, p=0.002), negatively with age (β=-0.35, p<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: LAGH demonstrates favorable therapeutic effects in ISS, and it holds the potential to benefit a greater number of Chinese pediatric patients affected by this condition.

title: Consensus Without the Difficult Questions: Clinical and Methodological Reflections on the International Idiopathic Short Stature Delphi Statements.
Predominant Mineralocorticoid Deficiency in ZNRF3-Related Adrenal Hypoplasia Congenita: A case report.
abstract: Introduction E3 ubiquitin protein ligase zinc and ring finger 3 (ZNRF3) negatively regulates Wnt/β-catenin signaling, which is essential for the development and maintenance of the adrenal gland, particularly the zona glomerulosa. Heterozygous ZNRF3 exon 2 deletions cause adrenal hypoplasia congenita (AHC). However, as only a few patients with ZNRF3-related AHC have been reported, the clinical spectrum remains unclear. Case Presentation A girl presented at age 27 days with severe salt-wasting. Endocrinological evaluation revealed elevated ACTH and renin levels. Abdominal ultrasonography failed to detect the adrenal glands. After treatment with hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone, she had no adrenal crises and normal growth and puberty. At age 15 years, hydrocortisone was discontinued, while fludrocortisone was continued. ACTH levels remained within clinically acceptable limits, whereas renin levels remained elevated. Whole-genome sequencing identified a ZNRF3 exon 2 deletion. Conclusion This is the first report of longitudinal endocrine findings in ZNRF3-related AHC, demonstrating predominant and persistent zona glomerulosa dysfunction with age-dependent improvement of zona fasciculata function. Our findings support the proposed role of the ZNRF3-Wnt/β-catenin signaling axis in adrenal development, expand the phenotypic spectrum of ZNRF3-related AHC, and suggest the value of genetic screening for ZNRF3 exon 2 deletions in patients with genetically unresolved mineralocorticoid deficiency.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Paediatric Endocrinology: A Narrative Review from the Perspective of Early-career Clinicians and Researchers.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) use by early-career paediatric endocrinologists has started without waiting for the training and governance structures to develop. Since early-career physicians and researchers of today hold no pre-AI performance baseline against which to appraise the AI outputs, career stage-specific concerns regarding rapid adoption of AI use in the field have emerged. The goal of this review was to examine AI use in paediatric endocrinology from the early-career perspective.
SUMMARY: A narrative, non-systematic literature review regarding the AI use in paediatric endocrinology across the four professional domains (curricular coverage, clinical practice, teaching, and research) was conducted in January 2026 and updated through July 2026. 57 relevant publications were identified, with level of evidence differing significantly between domains, and inversely with how freely the AI tools are used: from randomised-trials data regarding specific clinical applications like closed-loop insulin delivery and automated bone age assessment, to no published data regarding use of large language models in the research domain. Greatest benefit of automated bone age assessment in the early career stage was reported, while no published studies examining AI use by early-career paediatric endocrinologists were found.
KEY MESSAGES: While being most exposed to unsupervised AI use, early-career physicians are also the least studied group. Having in mind the lack of pre-AI baseline in this population, findings of this review emphasize the potential career stage-dependent risks regarding the AI use, and the need for subspecialty-specific AI competency frameworks.

title: When Less is More: A Physiology-Driven Approach to a 17-Hydroxylase Deficiency Case Series.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: 17-hydroxylase deficiency (17OHD) is a very rare form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) caused by autosomal recessive mutations in the cytochrome P450 family (CYP17A1). Despite low cortisol, adrenal insufficiency does not typically manifest because elevated corticosterone, a weaker glucocorticoid (GC), exerts GC effects. Exogenous GC are the foundation of treatment but can be associated with significant side effects. Published literature regarding management strategies is limited.
CASE PRESENTATIONS: We describe three female adolescents treated for 17OHD with different GC regimens. All patients presented at age 14 with delayed puberty, hypertension, and primary ovarian insufficiency. Patient 1 was initially treated with physiological hydrocortisone divided three times daily (10 mg/m2/d) and spironolactone 100 mg/d, separately and combined, which did not lower her blood pressure (BP). Eventually, a combination of physiological hydrocortisone once daily (8.8 mg/m2/d) and gradual titration to a higher spironolactone dose (100 mg bid) normalized her BP (115/75 mmHg) with no side effects. Patient 2 was treated with dexamethasone 0.25 mg daily for 10 years with poor follow-up and developed multiple complications related to supraphysiological GC use. She was transitioned and successfully treated with hydrocortisone 10 mg every morning and 5 mg every afternoon with a normal BP and potassium for over a year. Patient 3 was treated with cortisone acetate for 2.6 years and then with dexamethasone for about 10 months before discontinuation of GC and transition to spironolactone monotherapy. Her potassium and BP remained normal.
CONCLUSION: In conclusion, 17OHD is a rare form of CAH, with about 500 published cases and limited established management guidance. Our cases highlight the importance of considering the pathophysiology of 17OHD when developing a management plan; a supraphysiological GC therapy may not be necessary to manage the hypertension and hypokalemia. Physiological hydrocortisone dosing lowers but does not normalize DOC production allowing DOC to exert GC effects. Physiological hydrocortisone and/or monotherapy with mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists both mitigate GC-related side effects, avoid adrenal suppression, and minimize risk for adrenal crisis in patients with 17OHD.

title: Pregestational maternal diabetes primes neonatal beta cell dysfunction with structural remodelling, impaired calcium buffering and altered mTORC2-Gαq-PKCα signalling in a pig model.
abstract:
AIMS/HYPOTHESIS: Offspring of mothers with diabetes are at increased risk of developing type 2 diabetes, and this predisposition is established during fetal life. The aim of this study was to define the functional, morphological and molecular alterations in neonatal pancreatic islets associated with maternal hyperglycaemia, with a particular focus on beta cells, an area that remains poorly understood. Given its similarity to humans in endocrine pancreas development, the pig was used as a translational animal model.
METHODS: Using genetically diabetic and beta cell reporter pig models, we performed functional assessments of glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in vivo and in situ using fresh pancreatic tissue slices from neonatal piglets born to hyperglycaemic mothers (PHGs) or normoglycaemic mothers (PNGs). Morphological and molecular profiling, including proteomics and single-cell RNA-seq, were performed to elucidate molecular changes reflecting the developmental impact of maternal diabetes on offspring metabolic health, with a particular focus on neonatal beta cells.
RESULTS: PHGs were born hyperglycaemic, hyperinsulinaemic and insulin resistant, exhibiting markedly delayed glucose and insulin response curves following oral glucose administration, with more pronounced effects in male piglets. Elevated basal insulin secretion and an almost blunted glucose responsiveness of pancreatic tissue slices were associated with increased insulin and somatostatin content, expansion of beta (+35%) and delta (+47%) cell populations, and organisation into larger islet clusters. Neonatal PHG islets exhibited a molecular profile consistent with intrinsic beta cell dysfunction that partially overlapped with type 2 diabetes (e.g. RBP4 upregulation), together with alterations in glucose sensing (near absence of GLUT2), nutrient metabolism resembling congenital hyperinsulinism (HADH downregulation), and cytosolic Ca2⁺ homeostasis (near absence of the Ca2⁺ buffer calbindin D28K). In addition to an ATF4-dominated stress signature, a shift towards a distinct PHG beta cell subcluster characterised by low expression of ribosomal genes was observed, with an adaptive early-response-gene-mediated transcriptional reactivity. In contrast to the Gαs-adenylyl cyclase-cAMP-PKA signalling axis that dominated in PNG beta cells, neonatal PHG beta cells displayed distinct alterations in Gαq-PLC-PKCα signalling components, the mTORC2 target PKCα, and CREB1, suggesting a restructured signalling architecture.
CONCLUSIONS/INTERPRETATION: Our findings reveal altered islet modelling with a unique beta cell dysfunction profile that partially overlaps with, but differs from, that of type 2 diabetes. A shift towards a beta cell subcluster exhibiting an adaptive early-response-gene-mediated transcriptional reactivity and an ATF4-associated transcriptional stress signature provides insight into molecular alterations associated with fetal exposure to maternal diabetes and may contribute to the increased risk of metabolic disease in offspring.

title: Co-creating the EndoWatch - a smart wearable device for the management of hypothalamic dysfunction in pediatric brain tumor survivors: a pilot study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hypothalamic dysfunction (HD) after treatment for a pediatric (supra)sellar tumor severely affects quality of life of patients, as well as their parents and families. Patients may develop signs of fatigue as a result of persistent disturbances in thermoregulation, sleep-wake rhythm, or hormonal insufficiencies. The management of HD requires around-the-clock care by the parent or caregiver. To support patients with HD and their parents/caregivers, we co-created a smart wearable device for continuous monitoring (EndoWatch) to detect early signs of hypothalamic dysregulation. We aimed to evaluate adherence to and user experiences of the first EndoWatch design.
METHODS: In co-creation with clinicians, patient representatives, and design researchers and engineers, an existing smart device (wearable sensor and mobile application (app)) was adapted to a first design tailored for this purpose. In a prospective, observational study, 10 pediatric brain tumor survivors with HD (8 children; 2 adults) tested the first design of the device for 14 days. The primary outcome was adherence to wearing the EndoWatch. Secondary outcomes included usability, learnability, and desirability (through questionnaires), and barriers and facilitators (through semi-structured interviews).
RESULTS: Ten patients participated (8 children, mean age 10.8 (SD 3.5); 2 adults, aged 18.9 and 31.0 years). Median overall adherence was 99.4% (IQR 22.8); two patients discontinued early due to wristband-related discomfort. Key facilitators were ease of use of the device and reliable technical performance. Main barriers included the absence of a separate caregiver app and limitations of the patient diary. These findings informed design modifications for future improvements of the device.
DISCUSSION: The concept of the first EndoWatch design was considered acceptable and usable by patients with HD and their caregivers. This study identified key barriers and the modifications required for improvement, which were incorporated into a second EndoWatch design, to be evaluated in a larger prospective study.

title: Isolated Hyperchlorhidrosis Caused by Novel Biallelic CA12 Variants Mimicking Pseudohypoaldosteronism.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Isolated hyperchlorhidrosis (HYCHL; OMIM 143860) is caused by biallelic CA12 variants encoding carbonic anhydrase XII (CA XII), a transmembrane enzyme that mediates sodium and chloride reabsorption in sweat glands, leading to excessive salt loss. Clinically, HYCHL presents in infancy with recurrent hyponatremic dehydration secondary to excessive salt loss, often mimicking pseudohypoaldosteronism (PHA) or cystic fibrosis (CF).
CASE PRESENTATION: A 5-month-old girl presented with irritability, lethargy, poor feeding, severe hyponatremia (110 mEq/L), and hyperkalemia (7.1 mEq/L). Congenital adrenal hyperplasia was excluded by endocrine evaluation. Markedly elevated plasma renin activity and aldosterone initially suggested PHA; however, low urinary sodium excretion during hyponatremia indicated an extrarenal source of salt loss. Three further episodes occurred, predominantly during summer. Although the parents consistently reported a salty taste of the infant's skin. Clinical exome sequencing identified two unreported compound heterozygous CA12 missense variants, c.823C>T p.(Arg275Trp) and c.694C>A p.(Pro232Thr), with parental testing confirming trans inheritance. No pathogenic variants were detected in CFTR or PHA-associated genes. By 19 months of age, the patient had remained free of hyponatremic episodes for nine months without disease-specific treatment, with normal growth and neurodevelopment.
CONCLUSION: This case expands the mutational spectrum of isolated hyperchlorhidrosis by identifying two unreported variants in CA12 and highlights the importance of considering isolated hyperchlorhidrosis in infants with recurrent salt-wasting when routine evaluation does not support PHA or CF.
